\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Comparison}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Products.Comparison
\section{Overview}
Weighted interpolation and the sharp noise radius give quantitative comparison of the first and second norms. Scalar estimates isolate the explicit constants used in finite-product anticoncentration, KKL bounds, and junta approximation.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Variance bound by noisy total influence]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ComparisonAux.variance_rpow_ratio_le_noisy_total}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteNorms.weighted_rpow_mean_le, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.component, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.totalInfluence, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.variance, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationAux.totalInfluence_eq_sum_card_components, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationAux.variance_eq_sum_components}
\difficulty{5}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom
masses, and let $f$ be a real-valued function on its outcome space with
$\operatorname{Var}_P(f)>0$. For every $\rho>0$,
$\operatorname{Var}_P(f)\,\rho^{I(f)/\operatorname{Var}_P(f)}\le\sum_S
|S|\rho^{|S|}\mathbb E_P f_S^2$, where the sum is over all coordinate sets $S$, $f_S$ is
the $S$-component, and $I(f)$ is the total influence.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Interpolation between product norms]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ComparisonAux.norm_interpolation_bound}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.mass, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.norm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lp_interpolation_cancel}
\difficulty{6}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom
masses, let $q,c\in\mathbb R$ with $q>2$, and let $f$ be a real-valued function on its
outcome space. If $\|f\|_{q,P}\le e^c\|f\|_{2,P}$, then $\|f\|_{2,P}\le
e^{cq/(q-2)}\|f\|_{1,P}$, where $\|f\|_{r,P}=(\mathbb E_P|f|^r)^{1/r}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Derivative of a logarithmic hyperbolic-sine difference]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ComparisonAux.log_sinh_difference_hasDerivAt_two}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For each real number $u>0$, the function $q\mapsto
\bigl(\log(\sinh(u/q))-\log(\sinh(u-u/q))\bigr)/2$ is differentiable at $q=2$, with
derivative $-u\cosh(u/2)/(4\sinh(u/2))$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Hyperbolic ratio of the log odds]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ComparisonAux.log_odds_coth}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
For a real number $\lambda$ satisfying $0<\lambda<\tfrac12$,
\[\frac{\cosh\!\left(\tfrac12\log\frac{1-\lambda}{\lambda}\right)}{\sinh\!\left(\tfrac12\log\frac{1-\lambda}{\lambda}\right)}=\frac{1}{1-2\lambda}.\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Limit of the sharp radius comparison]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ComparisonAux.sharp_radius_comparison_limit}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ComparisonAux.log_odds_coth, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ComparisonAux.log_sinh_difference_hasDerivAt_two, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.productNormComparisonConstant, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sharpDiscreteRadius}
\difficulty{6}
For $0<\lambda<1/2$, let $\rho(q,\lambda)$ be the sharp discrete radius and let
$C(\lambda)$ be the finite-product norm comparison constant as defined above. As $q$
tends to $2$ through values greater than $2$,
$\exp\!\left(-\frac{q\log\rho(q,\lambda)}{q-2}\right)$ tends to $C(\lambda)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Comparison constant at one half]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ComparisonAux.constant_tendsto_half}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.productNormComparisonConstant}
\difficulty{5}
Let $C(\lambda)$ equal $e$ when $\lambda=1/2$, and equal
$((1-\lambda)/\lambda)^{1/(2(1-2\lambda))}$ otherwise, with the real-power conventions
in its definition. As $\lambda$ tends to $1/2$ from below through values in $(0,1/2)$,
$C(\lambda)$ tends to $e$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Positive-support probability estimate]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ComparisonAux.centered_probability_ge_of_norm_comparison}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteNorms.centered_abs_sum_sq_le, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.indicator, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.mass, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.norm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.prob}
\difficulty{5}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces: each coordinate space has
strictly positive weights summing to one. For a real-valued function $g$ on the product
space, suppose its expectation is zero and its second moment is positive. If $C>0$ and
$\|g\|_{2,P}\le C\|g\|_{1,P}$, then $\frac{1}{4C^2}\le \Pr_P(g>0)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Coarse anticoncentration coefficient]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ComparisonAux.anticoncentration_coarse_lower_bound}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
For every real $\lambda>0$ and every positive integer $k$, $(15/\lambda)^{-k}\le
\frac14(e^2/(2\lambda))^{-k}$, where the exponents are real powers with exponent $-k$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[KKL coefficient identity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ComparisonAux.kkl_coefficient_eq}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $\lambda,V,I\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $\lambda>0$ and $V>0$. Then
\[
\left(\frac{V(\sqrt{\lambda}/3)^{I/V}}{I}\right)^2=\left((I/V)^{-1}\right)^2(9/\lambda)^{-I/V}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Bounds on logarithmic parameters]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ComparisonAux.kkl_log_parameters}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For a real number $\lambda$ with $0<\lambda\le 1/2$, the logarithms satisfy $\frac12\le
\log(1/\lambda)\le \log(9/\lambda)\le 5\log(1/\lambda)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Exponential inverse-square bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ComparisonAux.kkl_inverse_square_exp_lower}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For every positive real number $t$, $e^{-2t} \le (t^{-1})^2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Scalar KKL dichotomy]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ComparisonAux.kkl_scalar_dichotomy}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ComparisonAux.kkl_inverse_square_exp_lower}
\difficulty{5}
Let $L,D,x,t\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $2\le 100L$, $2(D+2)\le 100L$, $x\ge 0$, and $t>0$.
Then either $\frac{x}{100L e^x}\le \frac{t}{e^x}$ or $\frac{x}{100L e^x}\le
t^{-2}e^{-Dt}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Low degree mass outside a coordinate set]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ComparisonAux.lowDegree_omission_le_of_stable_bound}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteNorms.weighted_lowDegree_omission_le, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.component, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.influence, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.laplacian, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.totalInfluence}
\difficulty{5}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom
masses, let $f$ be a real-valued function on its outcome space, let $J$ be a set of
coordinates, and let $k$ be a nonnegative integer. Suppose $0\le\rho\le1$ and
$\tau\ge0$, every coordinate $i\notin J$ has influence at most $\tau$, and for every
coordinate $i$ the sum of $\rho^{|S|}\mathbb E_P f_S^2$ over coordinate sets $S$
containing $i$ is at most $I_i(f)^{3/2}$. Then $\rho^k$ times the sum of $\mathbb E_P
f_S^2$ over sets $S$ with $|S|\le k$ that are not contained in $J$ is at most
$\sqrt{\tau}\,I(f)$, where $f_S$ denotes the $S$-component, $I_i(f)$ the coordinate
influence, and $I(f)$ the total influence.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Influence cutoff and noise parameters]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ComparisonAux.junta_threshold_parameters}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $\lambda,I,\varepsilon\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $0<\lambda\le 1/2$, $I>0$, and
$\varepsilon>0$, and let $k\in\mathbb N$. Set $\rho=\sqrt{\lambda}/3$ and
$\tau=(\varepsilon/(2I))^2\rho^{2k}$. Then $0<\rho\le 1$, $\tau>0$,
$\sqrt{\tau}\,I=(\varepsilon/2)\rho^k$, and $I/\tau=(4I^3/\varepsilon^2)(9/\lambda)^k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Absorbing polynomial factors]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ComparisonAux.junta_polynomial_absorption}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ComparisonAux.kkl_log_parameters}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\lambda,I,\varepsilon$ be real numbers with $0<\lambda\le 1/2$, $0<\varepsilon\le
1$, and $\varepsilon\le I$. For every natural number $k$ satisfying $k\le
3I/\varepsilon$, we have
$\frac{4I^3}{\varepsilon^2}\left(\frac{9}{\lambda}\right)^k\le\left(\frac{1}{\lambda}\right)^{100I/\varepsilon}$.
\end{theorem}
